text.L1: A fraction names equal parts of one whole.
text.L2: The bottom number tells how many equal parts make the whole, and the top number tells how many we take.
text.L3: Here, one-half has two equal parts, while one-quarter has four equal parts.
text.L4: More equal parts make smaller pieces, so one-half is bigger than one-quarter.
text.L5: That busts the myth that a bigger bottom number makes a bigger fraction.
text.L6: A fraction of a collection also means sharing the collection into equal groups.
text.L7: To find one-third of 15 pencils, share them into three equal groups.
text.L8: Each group has 5 pencils, so one-third of 15 is 5.

text.L1: Fractions are numbers, so they have places on a number line.
text.L2: The bottom number tells how many equal gaps to make from 0 to 1.
text.L3: Count gaps, not marks. Four marks between 0 and 1 make five equal gaps.
text.L4: So each gap is one fifth. The top number tells how many gaps to count from 0.
text.L5: To mark two fifths, count two gaps from 0. That mark is 2/5.
text.L6: A fraction can also go beyond 1. If the top number is bigger than the bottom number, it lies past 1.
text.L7: For example, 5/4 is one quarter past 1, so it is after 1.
text.L8: Now use these ideas to choose where 5/4 belongs.

text.L1: Fractions are numbers, so they have places on a number line.
text.L2: The bottom number tells how many equal gaps to make from 0 to 1.
text.L3: Count gaps, not marks. Four marks between 0 and 1 make five equal gaps.
text.L4: So each gap is one fifth. The top number tells how many gaps to count from 0.
text.L5: To mark two fifths, count two gaps from 0. That mark is 2/5.
text.L6: A fraction can also go beyond 1. If the top number is bigger than the bottom number, it lies past 1.
text.L7: For example, 5/4 is one quarter past 1, so it is after 1.
text.L8: Now use these ideas to choose where 5/4 belongs.

ask.text: What do you notice?

text.L1: Numbers can be sorted by pairing their things. A full set of pairs is even; one left over is odd.
text.L2: Here is a common mistake: 34 is not odd just because it contains the odd digit 3.
text.L3: Only the ones digit decides. Tens and hundreds make full pairs.
text.L4: Look at 247. Its ones digit is 7, and 7 makes three pairs with one left over.
text.L5: So 247 is odd. The same rule says numbers ending in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8 are even; 0 is even too.
text.L6: Now add two odd numbers, such as 3 and 5. Their two leftovers pair up, making 8, an even number.
text.L7: Even plus even is even, while odd plus even stays odd because one leftover remains.
text.L8: Your turn: tap the number that is even.
